skills.name: Dashboard Metrics Computation

testcases.name: computes average MTTR in minutes for incidents resolved within 7 days
counts incidents created in current calendar month

skills.capability: Implement pure functions that compute the four stat-card metrics (open incident count, 7-day MTTR, incidents this month, uptime %) from raw incident/component data.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing metric-computation utilities for an incident dashboard. Given arrays of incident objects (each with id, severity, state, created_at, resolved_at) and component uptime data, write pure, deterministic functions to compute open incident count, 7-day mean-time-to-resolve, incidents created in the current calendar month, and overall uptime percentage. Accept an explicit reference date parameter so results are testable without relying on the system clock.
acceptance_criteria: computeOpenIncidentsCount returns the count of incidents whose state is not 'resolved'
compute7DayMTTR returns the average resolution time in minutes for incidents resolved within 7 days of the reference date
computeIncidentsThisMonth returns the count of incidents created in the same calendar month/year as the reference date
computeUptimePercent returns a percentage between 0 and 100 derived from component uptime data

skills.name: Stat Cards UI Component
skills.capability: Build the four-stat-card row component that displays open incidents, 7-day MTTR, incidents this month, and uptime %, wired to the metrics computation functions.
skills.prompt_template: You are building the stat-card row for the internal incident dashboard. Render four cards — open incidents, 7-day MTTR, incidents this month, overall uptime % — using values from the metrics computation utilities. Match the dark-themed Figma design tokens for spacing, typography, and card styling, and ensure the cards re-render when incident data changes.
acceptance_criteria: StatCards component renders exactly four cards with correct labels
Each card displays the value returned by its corresponding metrics function
Component re-renders with updated values when the incidents prop changes
Card styling uses the dark theme design tokens (background, text, border colors) rather than hardcoded values

skills.name: Severity Color Mapping
skills.capability: Implement a pure function mapping incident severity (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3) to its exact design-token color, enforcing the constraint that these colors are reserved exclusively for severity indication.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing the severity-to-color mapping used by the incident timeline. Write a pure function that takes a severity string (SEV1, SEV2, SEV3) and returns the exact hex/token color defined in the Figma spec: SEV1 red, SEV2 orange, SEV3 yellow. This mapping must be the single source of truth so these colors are never reused elsewhere in the UI for non-severity purposes.
acceptance_criteria: severityColor('SEV1') returns the red token value
severityColor('SEV2') returns the orange token value
severityColor('SEV3') returns the yellow token value
No other UI element (buttons, links, other badges) reuses these exact severity color values for a non-severity purpose

skills.name: Severity Incident Timeline Component
skills.capability: Build the incident timeline component that lists incidents in chronological order, color-coded by severity using the severity color mapping.
skills.prompt_template: You are building the severity-colored incident timeline for the internal dashboard. Render incidents in reverse-chronological order, using the severityColor mapping to color each timeline entry's indicator by SEV1/SEV2/SEV3. Ensure the component reads live incident data and does not hardcode colors outside the shared severity mapping.
acceptance_criteria: Timeline renders incidents ordered from most recent to oldest
Each timeline entry's severity indicator color matches the output of severityColor for that incident's severity
Timeline updates when the underlying incident data changes
No severity color is hardcoded inline outside the shared severityColor mapping

skills.name: State Chip Mapping & Component

testcases.name: open state maps to correct chip config
resolved state maps to correct chip config
unknown state throws rather than silently defaulting

skills.capability: Implement a pure function mapping exact DB incident state values (open/investigating/identified/resolved) to chip label/color, and the chip component that renders it.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing the state chip used to display an incident's current state. Write a pure function that takes the exact DB state string (open, investigating, identified, resolved) and returns its display label and design-token color, then build the chip component that renders this. The chip must reflect the literal DB state with no derived or inferred states.
acceptance_criteria: stateChipConfig('open') returns the correct label and color for the open state
stateChipConfig('investigating') returns the correct label and color for the investigating state
stateChipConfig('identified') returns the correct label and color for the identified state
stateChipConfig('resolved') returns the correct label and color for the resolved state
StateChip component renders the label and color returned by stateChipConfig for a given incident's state prop

skills.name: Dashboard Data Fetching & Live Refresh
skills.capability: Implement the data-fetching layer that loads incident data from the backend API into the dashboard so stat cards, timeline, and chips reflect live DB state.
skills.prompt_template: You are wiring the internal dashboard to live incident data. Implement a data-fetching hook/service that retrieves incidents from the backend REST API on mount and on a refresh interval or event, exposing loading/error/data states to the stat cards, timeline, and state chip components. Ensure state chips always reflect the exact current DB state with no client-side caching drift.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard fetches incident data from the API on initial load
Fetched data is passed through to stat cards, timeline, and chip components without transformation that alters DB state values
A loading state is shown while the initial fetch is in flight
An error state is shown if the fetch fails

skills.name: Dark Theme Token Integration
skills.capability: Apply the Figma dark-theme design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) consistently across the stat cards, timeline, and chips to match the design spec.
skills.prompt_template: You are applying the dark-theme design tokens from the Figma spec to the internal dashboard's stat cards, severity timeline, and state chips. Ensure background, text, border, and spacing values are pulled from the shared token set rather than hardcoded, and that the resulting UI visually matches the Figma dark theme.
acceptance_criteria: Stat cards, timeline, and chips use shared dark-theme token variables for background/text/border colors
No component hardcodes a raw hex/color value outside the shared token set or the severity/state mappings
Rendered dashboard visually matches the Figma dark theme spec for spacing and typography
